## Scenario: Planning a Realistic 2-Level School Intervention Study

Real educational and organizational multilevel studies rarely fit textbook
idealized assumptions: cluster sizes vary across schools, researchers often
power for a **cross-level interaction** (e.g., whether a school-level
intervention `z1` moderates the slope of a student-level covariate `x1`), and
level-1 residuals can exhibit heavy tails.

This walkthrough takes a realistic study from plain English all the way to an
AST-verified standalone simulation script, executed power summary, visualization,
and reproducible study bundle—running 100% offline.

## 1. Plain-English Intent to Verified `spec_ir`

```{r}
library(specshiny)

prompt <- paste(
  "2-level power analysis for the cross-level interaction between x1 and z1 of 0.35",
  "with 40 schools, 18 students per school, cluster size sd 5, ICC 0.20,",
  "level-2 z1 effect 0.25, random slope for x1 with sd 0.20,",
  "t-distributed errors df 5, 12 replications"
)

tr <- nl_to_spec(prompt)
tr$spec
```

Inspect the synthesized mathematical model and LaTeX equation:

```{r}
math <- spec_to_math(tr$spec)
cat(math$formula, "\n\n")
cat(math$text, "\n")
```

## 2. Conversational Refinement with Undo/Redo History

Track design iterations with `spec_history()` as we add a cluster-count power
sweep across 25, 45, and 65 schools:

```{r}
hist <- spec_history(tr$spec)

ref1 <- refine_spec(tr$spec, "sweep clusters across 25, 45, 65")
history_push(hist, ref1$spec, label = "Add cluster count grid")
ref1$diff

# Inspect what happens if we also test 15% MAR attrition, then undo it
ref2 <- refine_spec(ref1$spec, "set 15% MAR missingness")
history_push(hist, ref2$spec, label = "Test 15% MAR")
history_summary(hist)

# Undo back to the complete-data sweep cleanly
restored <- history_undo(hist)
study_spec <- restored$spec
study_spec$missingness$mechanism
```

## 3. Dynamic Minimal UI Control Surface

Notice how `spec_to_controls()` automatically exposes ONLY the active
parameters for this complex design—including `cluster_size_sd`, `error_df`,
`inter_beta_x1__z1`, `slope_sd_x1`, `corr_1_2`, and `grid_n_clusters`—while
still hiding irrelevant controls like `n_obs`, `error_skew`, `missing_rate`, or
`outcome_link`:

```{r}
desc <- spec_to_controls(study_spec)
desc
```

## 4. Compiling, AST-Verifying, and Executing the Power Study

Compile `study_spec` into a standalone R script (automatically verified by
`verify_compiled_r_ast()`), execute it in a fresh isolated environment, and
inspect the empirical power table across cluster counts:

```{r}
sim_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".R")
code <- compile_r_script(study_spec, file = sim_file, run_on_source = TRUE)
verify_compiled_r_ast(code)

has_lme4 <- requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)
if (has_lme4) {
  sim_env <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
  invisible(capture.output(sys.source(sim_file, envir = sim_env)))
  power_tbl <- sim_env$results$summary
  power_tbl
}
unlink(sim_file)
```

## 5. Visualizing the Empirical Power Curve

```{r, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 3.8}
if (has_lme4 && requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(power_tbl, ggplot2::aes(x = n_clusters, y = power)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(color = "#264653", linewidth = 1) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(color = "#264653", size = 3) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0.80, linetype = "dashed", color = "#6e7f8d") +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "Cross-Level Interaction Power Curve (x1:z1)",
      subtitle = "Unbalanced clusters (SD = 5), random slope, Student-t(df = 5) errors",
      x = "Number of Schools (J)",
      y = "Empirical Power (alpha = 0.05)"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
}
```

## 6. Exporting a Verified Study Bundle

Package the validated specification, standalone script, Quarto report, and
SHA-256 manifest into a self-contained reproducible archive:

```{r}
bundle_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "specshiny_mlm_walkthrough_bundle")
export_spec_bundle(study_spec, bundle_dir, overwrite = TRUE)
verify_spec_bundle(bundle_dir)
unlink(bundle_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```
